laws.name: Criminal Code, general production order
laws.text: A judge or justice of the peace can order a person or company to produce documents or data in its possession or control, when there are reasonable grounds to believe they will be evidence of an offence.

sources.title: Criminal Code, s. 2, definitions (Justice Laws Website)

laws.name: Criminal Code, production order for transmission data
laws.text: A judge or justice of the peace can order a person or company to produce transmission data in its possession or control: when, how long and between whom communications happened, but not what they said. It takes reasonable grounds to suspect the data will help investigate an offence.

laws.name: National Intelligence Law, Articles 7 and 14
laws.citation: National Intelligence Law of the People's Republic of China (2017, amended 2018), arts. 7 and 14
laws.text: Requires all organizations and citizens to support, assist and cooperate with national intelligence work in accordance with law, and to keep confidential any secrets of that work they become aware of. Intelligence agencies can ask them for that support.

laws.name: e-Evidence Regulation (European Production Orders)
laws.text: An authority in one EU country can order an online service based in another to hand over user data in 10 days, or 8 hours in an emergency. Account details need a prosecutor's order; content, or who contacted whom and when, needs a judge and usually a crime carrying three years or more in prison.

status_note.text: Applies from 2026-08-18. It covers orders from one EU country to a provider established or represented in another; a country's own powers over providers based there are national law, which FinePrint hasn't reviewed yet. It binds providers of communications, hosting and other services that store user data (art. 3(3)); FinePrint doesn't assess per company whether a provider qualifies.

laws.name: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Arrest and Search), section 43
laws.text: Lets a judge summon any person thought to hold an object, including a document or computer material, to produce it when the judge finds that necessary or desirable for an investigation or trial.

laws.name: Federal Law No. 149-FZ on Information, Article 10.1
laws.citation: Federal Law of 27 July 2006 No. 149-FZ, art. 10.1 (as amended by No. 374-FZ of 6 July 2016)
laws.text: Requires internet services that handle users' messages to store data about their communications, and the messages for up to six months, in Russia; to give them to the authorities in cases set by federal law; and to give the security service what it needs to decode encrypted messages.

laws.name: CLOUD Act
laws.text: Requires providers of communication and cloud services to disclose data in their possession, custody or control under US legal process, whether it is stored in the United States or elsewhere.

sources.title: 18 U.S.C. § 2713, United States Code (govinfo)
sources.quote: regardless of whether such communication … is located within or outside of the United States

laws.name: FISA Section 702
laws.text: Directives issued under it require electronic communication service providers to give the government information for surveillance of people reasonably believed to be outside the United States. Repealed 2026-06-12; directives issued before then stay in effect until they expire.

status_note.text: Section 702 was repealed on 2026-06-12, when its last extension ran out. Directives issued before then stay in effect until they expire, and the government can still ask the FISA court to compel compliance with them.
